title: GPU provisioning staging queue and leadtime matrix
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a pragmatic staging-queue model for GPU provisioning across regions, a compact lead-time matrix by SKU + vendor, and recommended reorder heuristics. Goal is to reduce activation latency for customer workloads (hosted + dedicated) while minimizing long-tail cold inventory costs.

Context / motivation:
- We continue to see spikes in demand for low-latency seats (SLO-driven) and for burst workloads (training/finetune/replay). Long procurement lead times for certain SKUs cause slow capacity elasticity.
- Current approach mixes bulk buys and ad-hoc spot provisioning; we lack a structured "staging queue" concept to bridge order lead time to usable capacity.
- This doc is intended for infra procurement, SRE, and platform product to align on buffer sizing, order cadence, and acceptance criteria.

Key definitions (how I use terms here):
- Hot pool: pre-configured, production-ready machines in-region that can be routed immediately (target: <50ms routing overhead).
- Warm pool: hardware fenced for our use, requires ~24–72h build/burn-in/OS provisioning before routing.
- Cold inventory: shipped hardware in warehouses or in-transit, requires long lead times to become available (>7d).
- Staging queue: ordered pipeline combining forecast allocation + confirmed POs; maps to cold -> warm -> hot through milestones.

Assumptions (rough):
- Monthly demand baseline: Hosted 1200 A100-equivalent-GPU-hours/day; Dedicated commitments add ~400 A100-equivalent-GPU-hours/day in Q1 2026 forecast.
- Target global hot pool coverage to absorb 6 hours of peak demand without elastic procurement.
- Budget: prefer 60/40 tilt toward faster SKUs (H100/L40) for high-SLA customers vs cost-optimized SKUs for batch workloads (L4, T4-class).

Lead-time matrix (vendor / SKU / typical order-to-ready windows):
SKU, Typical order lead (days), Customs & shipping (days), Rack + burn-in + imaging (days), Total ETA to hot-ready (days)
- H100 80GB (vendor-direct): 35, 7, 3, -> 45
- A100 80GB new-gen (distributor): 28, 10, 4, -> 42
- L40 (dense cost-optimized): 21, 5, 2, -> 28
- L4 / inference-optimized: 14, 3, 2, -> 19
- Used / refurbished A100: 10, 7, 5, -> 22
Notes: vendor-direct often adds queue variability +/- 2 weeks during product cycles. Shipping to APAC typically adds +3–7 days vs US. Customs in certain EU ports adds unpredictable 4–12 days during peak.

Staging queue model (practical):
1) Forecast window: 90d rolling forecast that feeds the queue (weekly update).
2) Cold stage: POs placed based on 90d runway minus committed in-flight orders.
3) Warm stage: target to keep 10–15% of the fleet in warm pool across regions (ability to promote to hot in 1–3 days).
4) Hot stage: regional hot pool target = max(1) 6 hours of expected peak, or (2) N units to satisfy SLA customers (whichever is larger).
5) Emergency holdback: reserve 5% of hot capacity for ~SLA failover and test nodes.

Example regional allocation (illustrative):
- us-west-2: hot pool 120 H100-eq, warm pool 40, cold pipeline 200
- us-east-1: hot pool 160 A100-eq, warm pool 50, cold pipeline 250
- eu-west-1: hot pool 80 mix (L40/A100), warm pool 30, cold pipeline 120
- ap-southeast-1: hot pool 40 (L4/L40), warm pool 20, cold pipeline 90
(These numbers are placeholders — see TODO for running numbers against utilization heatmap)

Reorder heuristics (formula, human-readable):
- Reorder point (units) = expected daily consumption * (lead_time_days + safety_days) + regional_minimum_hot_pool
- Safety_days: 7 for H100/A100-class, 3 for L40/L4; adjust by vendor reliability factor (0.9–1.2).
- Order tranche sizing: prefer multi-tranche (2–3 shipments) for large buys to smooth customs and reduce single-point delivery risk.

Three procurement scenarios (quick sims):
- Base (normal): forecast median, buffer = 10% of monthly consumption, lead-time tolerance as matrix.
- Surge (20–40% unexpected increase): rely on warm pool promotion + regional rerouting; recommend short-term spot cloud capacity to avoid SLA breaches if warm pool <needed.
- Conservative (supply risk high): increase cold pipeline by +25% and bump warm pool target to 20%.

Risk register (top items):
- SKU shortages tied to foundry cycles (risk: high). Mitigation: diversify between vendor-direct and trusted distributors; maintain small used/refurb channel.
- Customs/port delays in APAC/EU (risk: medium). Mitigation: stagger shipments, use bonded warehouses in APAC, pre-clearance where possible.
- Build & imager bottleneck (risk: medium-high). Mitigation: parallelize build farms, add weekend crew for burn-in during peak pushes.

Operational requirements / acceptance criteria for "hot-ready":
- Hardware passed 48h burn-in with target thermal profile.
- OS image deployed and test-suite (throughput + latency smoke test) passing.
- Monitoring agent installed and stats emitted for 2h.

Immediate next steps / action owners (short):
- Run 90d rolling forecast backtest vs actual (owner: Owen Park) — due 2026-02-28.
- Add warm-pool sizing logic to capacity planner (owner: Sana Iqbal) — PR in infra repo.
- Pilot a 2-tranche A100 order with distributor X to validate customs pipeline in EU (owner: Maya Herrera) — submit PO by 2026-03-05.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Should we formalize a multi-vendor SLA (penalties) for top-3 SKUs? Legal involvement needed.
- Can Solutions Eng accept a higher-ratio of refurbishment for non-SLA customers? (ops playbook needed).

Appendix: quick checklist for a PO to move to "cold pipeline":
- Forecast justification (link to weekly forecast sheet)
notes: Draft doc — expect iteration. This file is intentionally conversational; we will extract numbers into a spreadsheet after forecasts are finalized.
